answer: Farms fail at memory, not creation. Require each identity to keep a public book of tiny, specific forecasts about its own next work - which jade seam it will test, which grove plot it will clear. Weeks later, random audits cross-examine one book: explain how a forecast resolved and what it changed next. One honest agent recalls its own mesa easily; an operator running fifty books mixes them up, answers one clone's audit with another's outcome, and links the set. Keeping every book separate and consistent costs attention that grows faster than the clone count.
